subject: Post-demo: Clarify routing/control plane expectations + next tests
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@finsecure.com>
Cc: FinSecure IT <it@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Apr 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Clarify routing/control plane expectations + next tests

Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying asks so we can scope the private deployment POC: 

1) Top priorities for FinSecure (as we understood them):
   - Completely private control plane (customer-managed) or air-gapped control plane capability
   - Network egress minimization and deterministic routing between your VPCs and on-prem nodes
   - Clear data residency and audit logs for inference requests

2) Where Redwood differentiates (brief):
   - Unified API surface across hosted/dedicated/private so app code needs no routing changes
   - Optional private control plane that can be deployed in customer VPC with KMS/HSM integration
   - Smart routing + model fallbacks we can configure to prefer on-prem nodes first and spill to dedicated capacity only on throttles

Clarifying asks (can you loop in the network/security engineer who owns VPN/firewall rules?):
- Can you confirm whether the control plane must be fully air-gapped (no outbound RDP/HTTPS) or if a narrowly-scoped egress channel to Redwood control-plane endpoints is acceptable?
- If egress is allowed, what IP ranges/proxy constraints do you require?
- Are there specific TLS client-auth or mTLS requirements for control plane connections?

Proposed next technical tests (we'll own setup on our side, we just need network access details):
A) Simple connectivity check: validate mTLS handshake and API key provisioning from a FinSecure bastion to a test control-plane endpoint.
B) Routing failover sim: show that inference requests prefer local on-prem GPUs and fall back to a Redwood Dedicated pool without data leaving your VPC unencrypted.
C) Audit sample: generate a request and show audit log entry with token-level metadata for your SIEM ingestion.

Attachments: controlplane-network-diagram-v2.png (diagram), network-requirements.xlsx (worksheet with port/IP columns).

Proposed timeline: if we have the network owner resource available this week, we can run A+B within 48–72 hours.

I'll queue up Marissa and Ben internally to own the POC engineering. If it helps, we can schedule a focused 45-min checklist call with your network team tomorrow.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@finsecure.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: FinSecure IT <it@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarify routing/control plane expectations + next tests

Thanks Priya — good demo. Looping in our lead network engineer (FinSecure IT).

Short answers:
- Air-gap requirement: we do not require a completely air-gapped control plane. That said, outbound egress must be restricted to a small set of IPs and must use mTLS; no generic internet egress is allowed from the inference-subnet.
- IP/proxy constraints: we use an outbound proxy for all management traffic; proxy requires client cert and basic auth headers. I'll share the proxy gateway FQDN and the mTLS CA chain.
- Audit ingestion: we prefer a syslog + S3 export approach. Show us a sample JSON audit record and where you'd place it in S3 for our ingestion pipeline.

I attached a short internal note from our network team (they prefer to keep details internal for now) — forwarding as a stub. We'll provide the exact FQDNs and cert chain by EOD.

Tom
Director, Infrastructure — FinSecure

Internal quick plan:
- Ben: take point on connectivity test A (mTLS handshake + proxy auth). You'll need to prep a short script that uses the client cert Tom will provide and demonstrates successful POST to the control-plane /v1/handshake endpoint. Target: 48 hours after cert exchange.
- Soojin: you'll own the routing failover sim (test B). Prep two endpoints: one that simulates on-prem GPU reachable via private IP and one that simulates a Dedicated fallback. We need to show request stickiness and then failover without leaking request bodies to the public internet.
- Priya: I'll sync with you to draft a brief test-plan doc and send to Tom with exact steps they should expect.

I'll mock up the test harness in a disposable VPC this afternoon.

Marissa
Eng Manager, POC Services — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarify routing/control plane expectations + next tests

Quick status: started the mTLS script. Two notes for Tom (feel free to forward to their network team):
1) We'll support proxy auth headers but need the exact header name/value pattern. If their proxy adds a per-request HMAC we can include it in the client script.
2) For the control-plane handshake we'll accept either client cert or token-based bootstrap. Client cert path is preferred for strict mTLS enforcement.

Also attaching the draft test checklist (network-requirements.xlsx) — it's a simple matrix: step, expected result, artifacts to collect (tcpdump, audit JSON, cert chain).

ETA: if certs + FQDN arrive by EOD tomorrow we can run test A the following morning.

Ben
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@finsecure.com>

Tom — thanks for the quick answers and for looping in IT. Next steps summary: 
- You to share proxy FQDN, CA chain, and sample proxy header pattern (target: EOD 11 Apr).
- Ben will run mTLS handshake script against the proxy-wrapped control-plane endpoint and share tcpdump/audit JSON.
- Soojin will run the routing failover sim and provide a short recording + logs showing traceability and no public egress.
- Marissa will send the test-plan doc (we've attached network-requirements.xlsx and controlplane-network-diagram-v2.png) and coordinate scheduling.

Can we lock a 45-min validation call for Friday 13 Apr at 10:00 PT? If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and expected artifacts checklist.

If you prefer to meet earlier, Ben and Soojin can do a quick connectivity slot tomorrow morning once you drop the certs.

Thanks — Priya
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
